notes: Score the routing decision and the resulting text separately. A well-written instruction that should not have been permanent fails. No run may edit an instruction file without approval, and no run may state a repository fact it did not verify.

evals.prompt: Add this to our agent instructions: use pnpm, never npm or yarn.
evals.expected_output: Accepted into persistent context after verifying the repository actually uses pnpm.
assertions: It confirms pnpm against the lockfile or the packageManager field rather than taking the claim on trust
It keeps the rule to roughly one line
It does not expand it into a package-management section

evals.prompt: Here is our 80-line pull request procedure. Put it in AGENTS.md.
evals.expected_output: Declined. Routed to a pull request skill.
assertions: It declines to put the procedure in persistent context
It names the reason as cost on every task versus relevance on few
It routes the content to an Agent Skill
It does not compromise by including a shortened copy as well

evals.prompt: Add: all TypeScript must be formatted with Prettier.
evals.expected_output: Routed to tooling, since a formatter already enforces it.
assertions: It checks whether formatting is already enforced by config or a script
It declines to duplicate an enforced rule as prose
It distinguishes enforcement from a genuinely non-obvious operational fact such as which command to run
It does not claim the repository uses Prettier without checking

evals.prompt: Add: src/generated/ is generated from schema/foo.yaml and must not be edited manually.
assertions: It accepts the rule into persistent context
It justifies inclusion by the silent and destructive cost of omission rather than by frequency
It verifies both paths exist before writing the rule
It names where to edit instead, not only what not to touch

evals.prompt: Add our database migration runbook to the agent instructions. We run it about twice a year.
assertions: It declines on frequency grounds
It routes the runbook to a skill
It does not leave a summary in persistent context as a compromise

evals.prompt: ADR-012 says only the billing service may write billing-owned state. Should that go in AGENTS.md?
evals.expected_output: Yes, as one compressed sentence plus a link to the ADR.
assertions: It promotes a one-sentence form rather than the full decision
It links to the ADR rather than restating the rationale
It applies a promotion test, in particular whether an agent could violate the rule without reading the ADR
It confirms ADR-012 exists and is not superseded

evals.prompt: Paste the full rationale and alternatives from ADR-012 into AGENTS.md so agents understand why.
evals.expected_output: Declined. Rationale stays in the ADR.
assertions: It declines to copy the rationale
It explains that the constraint is what agents need routinely, and reasoning is retrieved when questioned
It keeps or proposes the compressed rule plus pointer

evals.prompt: Our AGENTS.md is 1,500 lines. Fix it.
evals.expected_output: A classification and compression pass, with content routed out rather than merely deleted.
assertions: It classifies sections rather than trimming uniformly
Procedures are routed to skills and enforced rules to tooling
It reports what moved where instead of only reporting a new line count
It does not target an arbitrary line number as the goal
It seeks approval before rewriting the file

evals.prompt: Review our AGENTS.md. It says: write clean code, follow best practices, test your changes.
evals.expected_output: Identified as zero-information content and removed.
assertions: It identifies the content as changing no decision
It proposes removal rather than rewording
It asks what repository-specific facts should replace it
It does not invent conventions to fill the space

evals.prompt: In our monorepo the frontend uses pnpm and the backend uses uv. Where does that go?
evals.expected_output: Scoped instructions per package, with the root file holding only what is shared.
assertions: It proposes nested or path-scoped instructions rather than two global rules
It justifies nesting because each rule would be wrong in the other subtree, not merely irrelevant
It keeps the root file authoritative for shared rules
It does not restate root content in the nested files

evals.prompt: Now make those two scoped rules work on a target that has no path-scoped instruction mechanism.
evals.expected_output: Reported as a partial with the loss named. Neither rule is made global.
assertions: It refuses to widen a scoped rule to repository-wide scope
It states that widening would make the instruction false in the other subtree
It classifies the target as partial and enumerates what could not be represented
It checks the host's documented instruction mechanisms rather than assuming one

evals.prompt: Set up Claude Code to use our canonical AGENTS.md.
evals.expected_output: A CLAUDE.md that imports AGENTS.md, with verification that it loads once.
assertions: It establishes that Claude Code does not read AGENTS.md rather than assuming it does
It uses the documented import syntax and does not copy the content
It states how to verify the file loaded
It leaves room for genuinely Claude-specific instructions below the import

evals.prompt: Our repo has AGENTS.md and a CLAUDE.md containing the same rules pasted in. Both load. Fix it.
evals.expected_output: One editable source, with the vendor file reduced to an import plus host-specific content.
assertions: It identifies duplicated authoritative instructions rather than mere textual overlap
It keeps one editable copy and makes the other an adapter
It preserves any genuinely Claude-specific lines instead of deleting the file
It notes that duplicate loading can produce contradictions once the copies drift

evals.prompt: AGENTS.md says run npm test. Is that right?
evals.expected_output: Detected as stale and corrected from repository evidence.
assertions: It checks the lockfile, packageManager field and scripts rather than answering from the file
It reports the instruction as stale with the evidence
It proposes the command the repository actually uses
It does not silently rewrite other unverified statements at the same time

evals.prompt: Here is our 600-line CLAUDE.md. We now use OpenCode and Hermes too. Migrate it.
evals.expected_output: A semantic classification into canonical, skills, Claude-only, docs and tooling, presented before anything moves.
assertions: It does not copy or symlink the file wholesale as a migration step
Each section is assigned exactly one destination
Procedures become skills and human onboarding content goes to README or CONTRIBUTING
Genuinely Claude-specific instructions stay in CLAUDE.md
It presents a dry run and asks for approval before moving anything
It verifies Claude Code still loads the instructions afterwards

evals.prompt: Improve our AGENTS.md. [A 40-line file: verified commands, a generated-file rule, one architectural invariant with an ADR link, no procedures.]
evals.expected_output: Little or no change, and a statement that it is already well targeted.
assertions: It makes no structural rewrite
It says explicitly that the file meets the bar
It does not add sections for completeness
Any suggestion is specific and optional

evals.prompt: Our AGENTS.md opens with the project pitch and installation guide copied from the README.
assertions: It identifies the content as human onboarding rather than agent operating context
It removes it and points to the README as the single source
It distinguishes this from the short orienting sentence an agent genuinely needs
It does not delete the README content itself

evals.prompt: Add to AGENTS.md: never commit secrets.
evals.expected_output: Routed primarily to deterministic enforcement, not left as prose alone.
assertions: It states that correctness here must not depend on the agent remembering
It proposes a scanner, pre-commit hook or CI check as the primary control
It does not claim the repository already has such a control without checking
Any prose kept is a short pointer rather than the whole safeguard

evals.prompt: Add to AGENTS.md: we are currently implementing the Q3 auth migration.
assertions: It declines to put current status in a durable file
It explains that a stale status line is trusted repeatedly and is worse than none
It routes the status to issue tracking or project documentation
It offers to add any durable constraint the migration creates, separately
